name: English (MA)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
MA candidates must complete at least 45 units (usually nine courses) with a minimum 3.0 grade point average (GPA).

• Courses must be taken at the 200-level and above. At least two courses must be at the 300 level.

• Up to five units may be fulfilled with ENGLISH 398 Research Course.

• No more than two courses may be taken at the 100-level and must be approved by the Director of Graduate Studies.

• No more than two courses may be taken outside of the Department of English and must be approved by the Director of Graduate Studies.

• No creative writing courses may be used to fulfill the requirements.
rules.notes: Coterminal Master's Degrees describes university requirements for the coterminal MA.

rules.name: Required Courses
rules.desc: Complete at least 25 units in required coursework. Each course must be taken for 5 units. Students should take 10 units in pre-1800s literature, 10 units in post-1800s literature, and 5 units in theory or methodology.

children.name: English Literature Pre-1800
children.notes: Must take a minimum of 10 units.

children.name: English Literature Post-1800
children.notes: Must take a minimum of 10 units.

children.name: Course Option (20 units)
children.desc: A minimum of 20 units obtained by completing courses that represent a mixture of survey and specialized courses chosen to guarantee familiarity with a majority of the works on the qualifying exam reading list for doctoral candidates. Courses should be taken for a minimum of 3 units each.

children.name: Thesis Option
children.desc:
English MA students who can demonstrate particularly strong preparation in the history of English literature may petition to undertake a 40 to 60-page master’s thesis. Students may register for up to ten units of ENGLISH 399 Thesis.
Coterminal English M.A. students who pursue the thesis option may not pursue the English Honors program concurrently.
children.notes:
• A minimum of 15 units obtained by completing elective courses that represent a mixture of survey and specialized courses. Courses must be taken for at least 3 units each.

• Ten units of ENGLISH399 taken over two quarters.

children.name: Approved petition and 40 to 60-page master's thesis

rules.name: Research Course (OPTIONAL)
rules.desc: Up to five units of the 45 total units for the program may be fulfilled with ENGLISH 398.

blocks.name: Coterminal Program with School of Education

rules.name: Coterminal Program Overview
rules.desc:
Students interested in becoming middle school and high school teachers of English may apply for admission to the coterminal teaching program (CTP) of the Stanford Teacher Education Program (STEP) in the School of Education.
CTP students complete a unique English language, composition, and literature curriculum combining a full English major with supplemental coursework in subjects commonly taught in California public schools and a core program of foundational courses in educational theory and practice. They are then admitted to STEP for a fifth year of pedagogical study and practice teaching. Students who complete the curriculum requirements can enter STEP without the necessity of taking either the GRE or the usual subject matter assessment tests.
CTP students receive a BA in English, an MA in Education, and a California Secondary Teaching Credential at the end of five years.
Students usually apply to the coterminal teaching program at the end of their sophomore year or the beginning of their junior year. For complete program details and information on how to apply, consult the Director of Undergraduate Studies in English or the CTP coordinator in the School of Education.

transferPolicy: By university policy, the Department of English does not allow transfer credit for master’s students.
reviewNotes: You need 45 units: 10 units of pre-1800 literature, 10 of post-1800 literature and 5 of theory or methodology, each course taken for 5 units, plus either 20 units of 200-level English electives or the thesis option (an approved petition, 10 units of ENGLISH 399 and 15 elective units), with at least two 300-level courses. Electives must carry at least 3 units each, creative writing courses do not count, ENGLISH 399 counts only toward the thesis option, and at most 5 units of ENGLISH 398 count. Your advisor checks the 3.0 GPA, and the up to two 100-level or outside-department courses the Director of Graduate Studies approves are moved in by hand.
